testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How should pre-trip inspections be done?

options.text: Change what you check each time to focus on different items.
Do them the same way every time so you don't forget anything.
Do them once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them the same way every time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This routine helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you don't miss anything important.

questions.question: What does the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How fast you reach your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner scores you on specific driving moves and how well you drive in general during the on-road test.

questions.question: What may cause you to be denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) considers you a security threat.
You are a lawful U.S. citizen.
You work for a foreign company.
You do not have perfect vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) considers you a security threat.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if you are not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, have been convicted of certain crimes, have been judged mentally unfit, or are considered a security threat by the TSA.

questions.question: What is a header board used for?

options.text: To help a driver see behind the vehicle.
To protect the driver from moving cargo.
To keep the driver from leaving the tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the driver from moving cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board, also called a "headache rack," protects the driver from cargo that moves during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: What should you check when looking at the fifth wheel gap during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: The locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.correctAnswerText: The locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Check that the fifth wheel locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin shank during a trailer coupling inspection.

questions.question: What should you do when making an emergency stop?

options.text: Move your trailer to the right and stop.
Move your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight. You can use controlled braking or stab braking, but stay straight so you can still turn if needed.

questions.question: What are passive railroad crossings?

options.text: They have no traffic control devices.
They have gates that come down when trains come.
A commercial vehicle should never cross them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have no traffic control devices.
questions.explanation: Passive crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: Why should you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: The air gets old and needs to be replaced.
Compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks.
To change the pressure in the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air holds moisture and oil that build up in the tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks regularly, especially at the end of each driving day if there is a manual drain valve.

questions.question: What should you do when passing parked vehicles?

options.text: Watch for people getting out of vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for people getting out of vehicles.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. Someone may step out of a car or come out from between cars without looking. A driver may also start moving their vehicle without seeing you.

questions.question: How long do you have to tell your employer about a traffic conviction?
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer about any traffic violation within 30 days. You must also inform your state licensing agency within 30 days if the violation happened in another state. This rule does not apply to parking tickets.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Needed only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip, no matter how long or short.

questions.question: When exiting a bus, a driver must:
questions.explanation: When exiting a bus, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. Always hold the handrail when exiting. Not following this rule may cause you to fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: When making a left turn, you should start turning:

options.text: Before reaching the center of the intersection.
At or after reaching the center of the intersection.
After your rear wheels pass the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or after reaching the center of the intersection.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle due to the width of your truck.

questions.question: When checking brakes, a slack adjuster should move ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Check each slack adjuster by pulling it. It should move no more than about one inch from where the push rod is attached. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles driven, missing exits or signs, drifting from your lane, and feeling restless. Staying in your lane is a sign of good driving, not fatigue.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, the hoses should be:
questions.explanation: When inspecting power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for any leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: The safe maximum play on a 20-inch steering wheel is:
questions.explanation: A steering wheel with more than 10 degrees of play may be unsafe. On a 20-inch wheel, this equals about two inches of movement at the rim.

questions.question: Emergency brakes must use what kind of force?
questions.explanation: Emergency brakes must use mechanical force. Air pressure can leak away over time, so it cannot be relied upon for emergency braking.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, stopping distance:

options.text: Is longer than on a dry surface.
Is shorter than on a dry surface.
Is about the same as on a dry surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is longer than on a dry surface.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on slippery surfaces because tires have less grip.

questions.question: When should you slow down for a curve?
questions.explanation: Always slow to a safe speed before entering a curve. Slowing while in the curve can cause a skid.

questions.question: If one air system in a dual air brake system loses pressure:

options.text: Either the front or rear brakes will not work properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work properly.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one air system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work properly. If air pressure gets too low while driving, pull over and park as soon as you can.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle must have:

options.text: A fire extinguisher only when carrying hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only when traveling through remote areas.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged and rated fire extinguisher.

questions.question: A separate air tank in a vehicle with dual parking control valves can be used to:

options.text: Make the air brakes work better.
Fill the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: A separate air tank in a vehicle with dual parking control valves can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. This allows the driver to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts are:
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its cargo while keeping the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are extremely dangerous.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should not:

options.text: Try to get out of their way.

questions.explanation: When an aggressive driver confronts you, get out of their way. Do not provoke them with eye contact, racing, or refusing to move. Ignore any gestures meant to upset you.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air:

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high in the tanks. If this happens, something is wrong and a mechanic should check the system.

questions.question: Most drivers are least alert:
questions.explanation: Fatigue and lack of alertness are major dangers when driving at night. Most people are least alert at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: Reading a text message while driving is:

options.text: Allowed if you are not pulling a trailer.

questions.explanation: Sending and reading text messages while driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Before driving downhill, you should:

options.text: Use only the brakes to slow down.

questions.explanation: On a steep downhill, use the engine's braking power as your main way to control speed. Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail.

questions.question: Cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Can make a vehicle tip over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make a vehicle tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Keep cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: How can you avoid slowing down traffic when driving a large truck?

options.text: Pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your truck cannot keep up with other traffic, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What should you do if you drive through flowing water or a large puddle?
questions.explanation: Avoid driving through water if possible. If you must drive through water, slow down and shift to a low gear. Gently apply the brakes to keep water and mud out of the brake system.

questions.question: If there are two left turn lanes, which one should you use?

options.text: Trucks should not turn where there are two left turn lanes.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra space to turn left. Use the right turn lane to begin your left turn.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid being an aggressive driver?

options.text: Plan trips without allowing extra time for traffic.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Do not make hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make hand gestures at other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan your trip with realistic travel times and allow extra time for traffic. Do not tailgate. Do not drive slowly in the left lane or make hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems use alcohol?

options.text: To prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
To make the compressor run more efficiently.
To lubricate parts of the braking system.
To prevent rust from forming on air brake valves.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. This device adds alcohol to the braking system to stop ice from forming.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop if your brakes fail while driving downhill?

options.text: Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Use rumble strips to slow your vehicle.

questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill grade, find an escape ramp quickly. If no ramp is available, steer onto a flat or uphill road or open field to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects air tanks and the brake system from too much air pressure. It usually opens at 150 psi.

questions.question: When checking engine belts during a vehicle inspection test, what must you do?

options.text: Check belts for tightness, allowing up to three inches of play.
The water pump belt does not need to be identified.
Identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.

questions.correctAnswerText: Identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for cracks and tightness. Allow up to three-quarters inch of play. If any of these items are not belt-driven, identify them and check that they work properly and are not damaged, leaking, or loose.

questions.question: As a truck driver, you are responsible for all of the following, except:

options.text: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your route.
questions.explanation: You must inspect cargo, recognize overloading or poor weight balance, ensure cargo is secured and does not block your view, and check that cargo does not block emergency equipment. You are responsible for your cargo even if someone else loaded it.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire fails while driving?

options.text: Keep one hand on the wheel and wave to other drivers with your other hand.

questions.explanation: If a tire fails, braking can cause you to lose control. Unless you must brake to avoid a crash, stay off the brakes until your vehicle slows down. Then brake very gently, pull over, and stop.

questions.question: When loading cargo, it is important to:

options.text: Stack items as high as possible.
Know the weight limit your vehicle's suspension system can handle.
Place light items underneath heavier items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know the weight limit your vehicle's suspension system can handle.
questions.explanation: As a driver, you must make sure your vehicle is not overloaded. You need to know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can safely carry, including its suspension system limit.

questions.question: When stopping:

options.text: Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly.
Press the brake pedal down quickly.
Pump the brake pedal repeatedly instead of holding it down.
Use the same amount of brake force every time you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down smoothly and gradually every time you slow or stop. The amount of brake pressure you need depends on how fast you are going and how quickly you need to stop.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: A driver who is color blind.
A person who does not know traffic rules.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. Stopping at a green light is one sign that a driver may be impaired.

questions.question: If your personal vehicle license is revoked or suspended:

options.text: You can get a hardship license to operate a commercial vehicle.
You cannot get a hardship license to operate a commercial vehicle.
Your commercial driver's license will not be affected.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot get a hardship license to operate a commercial vehicle.
questions.explanation: If your personal vehicle license is revoked, canceled, or suspended, you cannot get a hardship license to operate a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What is often found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in a brake system usually contains water and compressor oil. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact or gesture at them. Report them to authorities when you can do so safely.

questions.question: If you do not know how to put out a vehicle fire, you should:
questions.explanation: If you do not know which fire extinguisher to use on a vehicle fire, especially one involving hazardous materials, wait for firefighters to arrive and let them put it out.

questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer during your vehicle inspection, check the front for damage such as cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: If your wheels spin when accelerating on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Take your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: If your drive wheels spin while accelerating on a slippery surface, remove your foot from the accelerator.

questions.question: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is:

options.text: Acceptable if weather conditions are clear.

questions.explanation: Using a hand-held mobile device while operating a commercial vehicle is illegal and dangerous.
